svg.title: Isentropic compression of HFC-134a on the SI P–H chart
svg.text: HFC-134a: isentropic compression from −25 °C to the 26 °C saturation pressure
P–H diagram of HFC-134a, Figure 8(b2) attached to the paper (reference h = 200 kJ/kg, s = 1.00 for sat. liquid at 0 °C), redrawn section
isotherms in °C (violet); isentropes, s in kJ/(kg K) (red, labelled at their lower ends)
Start on the saturated-vapour line at −25 °C (0.106 MPa): H₂ = 383.45 kJ/kg, S₂ = 1.746 kJ/(kg K) (Table 9.1).
Follow the constant-entropy line s = 1.746 (between the 1.70 and 1.75 lines, close to 1.75) upwards …
… until it meets the condenser pressure, 0.685 MPa (saturation pressure at 26 °C); the vapour is at about 35 °C.
Drop vertically to the enthalpy axis: H₃′ ≈ 422 kJ/kg, so (ΔH)_S = 422 − 383.45 = 38.4 kJ/kg.
Dashed grey: the rest of the cycle (condensation to 235.97, throttling, evaporation). Quality lines x = 0.2 … 0.8 inside the dome.
Redrawn section from tabulated R-134a data (Çengel A-11 to A-13, IIR reference); in the exam read the printed chart.
